case.claim_text: New York winters are getting warmer

variable.label: Air temperature
variable.definition: How warm the air is about 2 m above the ground.
variable.caveat: Reanalysis: a weather model steered by observations, not a single thermometer.

steps.title: Monthly data
steps.detail: Monthly air temperature for New York, United States from NASA POWER, 1982–2025.

steps.title: Pick the season
steps.detail: Only the months the claim is about are kept (Dec, Jan, Feb).

steps.title: One value per year
steps.detail: The months of each year are averaged into one number.

steps.title: Overall direction
steps.detail: The typical change over time, robust to single extreme years (Sen's slope).

steps.title: Could it be chance?
steps.detail: Very unlikely to appear by chance if nothing were changing.

steps.title: Does the choice of years matter?
steps.detail: We repeat the check with the start and end shifted by a few years; at least 4 of 5 must agree.

steps.title: Ground station check
steps.detail: Ny City Central Park weather station, 8.4 km away. It changes at about the same pace as the satellite-model data.

steps.title: Verdict
steps.detail: The result depends on which years you pick.

extrapolation.note: What-if line, not a forecast: it only shows where the trend would go at this pace. For physically based futures see the climate-model scenarios.

scenarios.source: NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 (4-model ensemble: ACCESS-CM2, IPSL-CM6A-LR, MIROC6, MPI-ESM1-2-HR)
scenarios.note: These are climate-model scenarios, not a forecast. Which one happens depends on what people do.
